chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from Ḥarīz, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
That he was asked about the son of a woman taken by force: a man slanders him and says, “O son of the fornicatress,” so he عليه السلام said:
“I hold that the hadd applies to him: eighty lashes, and that he must repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for what he said.”

key_terms.الْفَاعِلَةِ: a woman accused here of illicit sexual conduct
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً: eighty lashes as the fixed hadd penalty
key_terms.يَتُوبُ: he must repent and turn back to Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on falsely calling someone the son of a fornicatress in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who falsely insults another with an accusation tied to illicit sexual conduct. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that the speaker is liable to the hadd punishment of eighty lashes and must repent to Allah عزّ وجلّ for his statement.
